ideas: Who you argued with and what it was about
How you made up and what changed

phrases.phrase: see it from their point of view

phrases.meaning: talk openly to end bad feelings

model: The argument I want to talk about was with my flatmate, Minh, about a year and a half ago, and it was about something really silly, the housework. We'd been sharing an apartment for about six months, and I felt I was doing most of the cleaning. One Sunday I was washing a huge pile of dishes that he'd left in the sink, and I just lost my temper. When he came home, I started complaining, and the conversation got heated very quickly. First, he said I was exaggerating. Then he pointed out that he always paid the bills and fixed things around the flat, which I hadn't really thought about. After that, we both said a few things we regretted, and he went out and didn't come back until late. For a couple of days we barely spoke, and I was worried we'd had a real falling-out. In the end, I decided to clear the air. I bought some bánh mì, knocked on his door and suggested we talk properly. Once I tried to see it from his point of view, I realised we just had different ideas of what was fair. We agreed to meet each other halfway and made a simple rota for the chores. So we made up, and we're still good friends today. In hindsight, I think we should have talked about it much earlier, instead of letting it build up.
